SMTO-EXE-0117 — The web page changed before SMTO could act

GUID: 8f3776cc-50b7-54a3-acb1-3f473d7d812f
Slug: browser-element-stale
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The page changed after SMTO looked at it, for example it reloaded or updated itself. To avoid clicking the wrong thing, SMTO did not click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "Look at the page again, then continue." SMTO needs a fresh look because its earlier view of the page is out of date.
  2. If the page keeps changing, such as a live feed, a timer or something still loading, wait until it settles, then ask SMTO to continue. A constantly changing page can make SMTO's view out of date again before it acts.
  3. Check that the page still shows what you expect. If it moved to another page, tell SMTO where it should be. A page change can mean an earlier step already took you somewhere else.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the click or typing on the refreshed page without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the web address, to the person who manages SMTO. Pages that update many times a second may not work well with SMTO's browser.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A saved browser element reference was missing or disconnected, or the page's revision changed between inspection and action, so the reference was discarded.

What this means

  • A saved element handle was missing/disconnected or the page revision changed while discovering or preparing its action. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • A saved element handle was missing/disconnected or the page revision changed while discovering or preparing its action.

How to diagnose it

  • Obtain current page metadata/snapshot and compare the intended control with its new exact reference; inspect any prior attempted action first.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._elements, _target, read_page and execute compare the tab's page revision before and after inspection and before mark(); DOM changes or navigation invalidate all element_refs, and a missing or disconnected handle raises element_stale. No click or input was dispatched. Take a fresh browser.snapshot or browser.find and use the newly returned element_ref; never reuse a ref after this error.
  • Inspect the page and prior action state, then obtain a fresh snapshot/find reference for the intended control.

Retry and execution caution

  • Take a new browser.snapshot or browser.find and retry using the new element reference.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh exact element remains connected through pre-action validation before separately justified interaction.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
